practice_questions.text: Read the extract where Mrs Johnstone reveals the twins’ identity at the Town Hall. How does Russell use language and dramatic techniques to present the tragedy? [40]
practice_questions.marks:
Top band (33–40) Analysis of Mickey’s ‘Why didn’t you give ME away?’ — grief, not selfishness. The gun as motif (toy to weapon). Mrs Johnstone’s desperate revelation. Cyclical structure: death at start and end. Context: class as the true killer.

Upper-mid band (25–32) Detailed analysis.

Mid band (17–24) Some valid points.

Lower-mid band (9–16) Basic comments.

Lower band (1–8) Simple awareness.

practice_questions.text: Write about how Russell builds towards the tragic ending elsewhere in the play. [40]
practice_questions.marks:
Top band (33–40) Traces foreshadowing from opening death scene, through ‘shoes upon the table’ motif, toy guns, Mickey’s decline, the affair. Every scene builds inevitability. Cyclical structure makes the ending feel both shocking and predetermined.

Upper-mid band (25–32) Thoughtful response.

Mid band (17–24) Some understanding.

Lower-mid band (9–16) Limited response.

Lower band (1–8) Brief comments.

practice_questions.text: Read the extract where Mickey tells Linda he needs the pills. How does Russell present Mickey’s mental state in this extract? [40]
practice_questions.marks:
Top band (33–40) Mickey’s short, defeated sentences. ‘They make me invisible’ — pills erase rather than heal. Contrast with childhood energy. Russell’s critique of how the system treats working-class depression.

Upper-mid band (25–32) Clear analysis.

Mid band (17–24) Some relevant points.

Lower-mid band (9–16) Basic comments.

Lower band (1–8) Simple awareness.

practice_questions.text: Write about how Russell presents the effects of the class system on individuals elsewhere in the play. [40]
practice_questions.marks:
Top band (33–40) Mrs Johnstone (poverty, coerced into giving up child), Mickey (unemployment, depression, prison), Linda (trapped between two men shaped by class), Sammy (crime as a product of deprivation). Class damages everyone in the play.

Upper-mid band (25–32) Thoughtful response.

Mid band (17–24) Some understanding.

Lower-mid band (9–16) Limited response.

Lower band (1–8) Brief comments.

practice_questions.text: Read the extract where Mrs Johnstone sings ‘Tell Me It’s Not True.’ How does Russell use this song to present grief? [40]
practice_questions.marks:
Top band (33–40) The song as lament over dead sons. Repetition of ‘tell me’ shows desperate denial. Cyclical structure: mirrors the Marilyn Monroe song’s crushed hope. Musical form intensifies emotion beyond what speech could achieve.

Upper-mid band (25–32) Detailed analysis.

Mid band (17–24) Some valid points.

Lower-mid band (9–16) Basic comments.

Lower band (1–8) Simple awareness.

practice_questions.text: Write about how Russell presents Mrs Johnstone’s suffering throughout the play. [40]
practice_questions.marks:
Top band (33–40) Abandoned by husband, coerced by Mrs Lyons, fired, watches Mickey’s decline, loses both sons. Russell positions her as the play’s moral heart — a good woman destroyed by a bad system. ‘Tell Me It’s Not True’ is the culmination of all her suffering.

Upper-mid band (25–32) Thoughtful response.

Mid band (17–24) Some understanding.

Lower-mid band (9–16) Limited response.

Lower band (1–8) Brief comments.
